S18.01.note: The title is generated in apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/lib/persist-message.ts; there is no visible control for it, so the tester only sees the result.
steps: Sign in and start a new chat without naming it.
Send one message and wait for the reply.
Look at the sidebar row for this chat and at the title at the top of the chat. Compare with Expected: a meaningful title, not a placeholder.
S18.01.where: No control. The title is written by the server after the first message; check the conversation's row in the sidebar list.

S18.02.note: A double-click on a sidebar row also starts renaming (packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/SessionItem.tsx) but that row has no visible label.
steps: Open a conversation that has messages.
Click the conversation title at the top of the chat.
Click Rename in the menu, type a new name and press Enter.
Open the sidebar and check that the row shows the new name; reload the page and check it again.
S18.02.where: Chat screen > conversation title at the top > Rename

steps: Hover a conversation row in the sidebar and click its three-dot More options button.
Click Pin.
Check that the row now shows a pin mark and moves to the top of the list (the move to top was not confirmed in the code read).
Repeat the menu and click Unpin; check the pin mark is gone.
S18.03.where: Sidebar > the row's More options button (three dots, hover the row) > Pin; later the same menu > Unpin

S18.04.note: The toast text Chat archived and its Undo button exist in packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/v3.json.
steps: Hover a conversation row, click its three-dot More options button and click Archive.
Check that the chat leaves the main list and a toast says Chat archived.
Click Show archived chats in the sidebar to list archived chats.
Click More options on the archived chat, click Restore, and check it returns to the main list. The chat screen menu also offers Archive and Unarchive.
S18.04.where: Sidebar > a row's More options button > Archive; to bring it back open Show archived chats and use the row's More options > Restore

S18.05.note: 'Disappears everywhere' (other devices) was not checked in the code read.
steps: Hover a conversation row, click its three-dot More options button and click Delete.
Read the dialog title Delete conversation? and its text; click Cancel first and check the chat is still there.
Click Delete again, then the Delete conversation button in the dialog.
Check the chat is gone from the sidebar and that opening its old link shows it as not found.
S18.05.where: Sidebar > a row's More options button > Delete, or chat screen > conversation title > Delete

S18.06.note: The menu says Duplicate as branch, not Duplicate; the code calls the fork action for it.
steps: Open a conversation that has messages.
Click the conversation title at the top of the chat and click Duplicate as branch.
Check that a new conversation opens with the same messages.
Send a message in the new one and check the original conversation is unchanged.
S18.06.where: Chat screen > conversation title at the top > Duplicate as branch

steps: Make sure at least one project exists (the menu item appears only when a project exists).
Hover a conversation row, click its three-dot More options button and open Move to project.
Click a project name.
Open that project and check the conversation is listed there.
S18.07.where: Sidebar > a row's More options button > Move to project > the project name; or chat screen > conversation title > Move to project

S18.09.note: The switch is disabled while a reply is still running.
steps: Open a new or existing conversation and look at the switch under the message box.
Click Work, then send a message.
Check the reply uses the work mode: the Work session panel opens from Panels.
Click Chat, send another message, and check it behaves as a chat reply.
S18.09.where: Composer (bottom of the chat) > second row > the Chat / Work switch

S18.10.note: The + button's own label was not located in the code read; the explanation text is in apps/web/lib/temporary-chat-policy.ts.
steps: Click the + button in the message box.
Click Use incognito and read the explanation under it: Stays out of your history, search, memory and Library.
Send a message and check the chat is not in the sidebar history after you leave it.
Open the + menu again and click Exit incognito (or End temporary chat) and check the state changes.
S18.10.where: Composer + button > Use incognito (switch to Exit incognito); the same menu shows End temporary chat

steps: Open a conversation with several messages.
Press Command+F.
Type a word that appears in the chat and check the Search messages... box opens.
Check the match count next to the box (N of M matches or No matches) and that matches are highlighted.
S18.11.where: Keyboard: Command+F (Ctrl+F on Windows/Linux) in an open chat > Search messages box

steps: Search for a word that has several matches.
Press Enter or click the Next match (Enter) arrow; check the view scrolls to the next match.
Press Shift+Enter or click the Previous match (Shift+Enter) arrow; check the view goes back.
Check the count in the box changes with each move.
S18.12.where: Search messages box (after Command+F) > Next match and Previous match arrows

S18.15.note: The rule for when the button appears was not traced in full.
steps: Open a long conversation and scroll up to an older message.
Look for the round down-arrow button at the bottom of the message area.
Click it and check the view jumps back to the latest message.
S18.15.where: Chat screen > round down-arrow button labelled Scroll to bottom (appears when you scroll up)

S18.17.note: The action buttons may only appear on hover or focus; the tester should look for them when hovering a reply.
steps: Hover an assistant reply and click Branch conversation from here.
Check a new branch is created for that point.
Find the branch arrows on the message that has branches and click Next branch and Previous branch.
Check the message content and the rest of the conversation change to the chosen branch.
S18.17.where: Hover an assistant reply > Branch conversation from here; then the branch arrows on that message (Previous branch, Next branch)

S18.18.note: The download button's exact text was not read; the Download icon is used there.
steps: Open a conversation and click the conversation title at the top.
Click Export….
In the Export Chat History dialog, pick Markdown, PDF or JSON and read the preview.
Click the download control and open the saved file; check it holds the whole conversation.
S18.18.where: Chat screen > conversation title at the top > Export…

S18.19.note: The dialog's create-link button text was not read.
steps: Open a conversation and click the conversation title, then Share….
In the Share conversation dialog, choose Anyone with the link and create the link using the dialog's button.
Copy the link.
Open the link in a private browser window without signing in and check the conversation shows.
S18.19.where: Chat screen > conversation title at the top > Share…, or the header button Share conversation

S18.20.note: When several links exist the title is Conversation links and the button is Revoke every link.
steps: Create a share link for a conversation (see S18.19) and reopen the Share conversation dialog.
Check the dialog shows the existing link state (title Public link ready or Shared with your workspace).
Click Revoke share, then the Revoke share confirmation in the dialog.
Open the old link in a private window and check it no longer opens.
S18.20.where: Share conversation dialog (open it again from Share…) > Revoke share

S18.21.note: The code shows no row for the conversation id or project; Expected lists both.
steps: Open a conversation with messages.
Click the Panels button at the top right and then Open Chat details.
Scroll to the Details section.
Check the rows Created, Last updated, Model (or Models) and Messages against the chat.
S18.21.where: Panels button (top right of the chat) > Open Chat details; the Details section is at the bottom of the panel

labels.text: Tools and files this session uses show up here.

S18.22.needs: a conversation that used files or web search
S18.22.note: No visible token budget, instructions or memory section was found in the panel code read.
steps: Open a conversation and click Panels, then Open Chat details.
Look at the Context section; in Work mode an empty section shows Tools and files this session uses show up here.
Look at the Sources section if the answer used web results.
Check the listed items match what the chat used.
S18.22.where: Panels button (top right of the chat) > Open Chat details > Context and Sources sections

S18.25.note: No visible on/off control for Web search was found; the code keeps it on automatically. A Run code toggle is passed to the + menu as a prop but no row for it was found in the menu.
steps: Open a conversation and click the + button in the message box.
Turn on Deep Research and send a message.
Send a second message in the same conversation and check Deep Research is still on.
Check the send preview lists Deep Research and, where shown, Web search.
S18.25.where: Composer + button > Deep Research (a switch); Web search is automatic for models that support it

S18.26.note: When the connector release is off the row shows Coming soon and is disabled; the per-conversation scope is set in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx; the surface is marked unfinished for ui in the plan.
steps: Connect a connector in Settings first, then open a conversation.
Click the + button and open Connectors.
Turn one connector off for this conversation and send a message.
Check the reply does not use it, then open the same menu in a different conversation and check it is still on there.
S18.26.where: Composer + button > Connectors > a connector name (switch per connector); Manage in Settings for the full list

S18.27.note: The dock opens itself for each Work run; the Expected asks for a list of tasks started from the conversation, which the dock shows only for the current run.
steps: Switch the composer to Work and send a task.
Click Panels at the top right and then Open Work session dock.
Read the Progress section and the status text (Ready, Paused or Finished with errors).
Compare the steps and status with the run that is still going.
S18.27.where: Composer > Work mode > Panels button > Open Work session dock; the dock lists Progress, Outputs and the run status

S18.28.needs: a second device or browser signed into the same account
S18.28.note: The code shows server-side saving only (persist-message.ts and the sidebar row); no visible continue control was found.
steps: On device A, start a conversation and send one message.
On device B (another browser or computer) sign in to the same account and find the conversation in the sidebar.
Open it, send a follow-up and check device A shows the new message after a refresh.
S18.28.where: Sidebar conversation list on a second device signed into the same account; no control for it.
